verification_report.summary:
The v2 proof is correct relative to the expressly preserved audit semipositive_dual_attainment_01 for the unchanged existence, trace-saturation, local regularity, exact-equation, and support inputs. The new argument is valid: for w=max(u,v), extended ordered contact applied to u<=w and v<=w gives the two disjoint lower bounds on {u>=v} and {u<v}; non-pluripolar extended measures and f dV ignore the common pole set, so w is a genuine threshold subsolution. The previously established local formula then gives omega+ddc u=omega+ddc v=omega+ddc w=a gamma on X minus Z.

For q=u,v, S=ddc(w-q) is real, closed, order zero (therefore normal), and supported on Z. With p=n-1, Demailly's support corollaries give S=sum c_j[Z_j] after eliminating the lower-dimensional remainder. At a generic smooth point of each divisor, Poincare–Lelong identifies c_j=nu(w,Z_j)-nu(q,Z_j); w>=q makes c_j<=0. Pairing with any smooth strictly positive Gauduchon metric yields 0=sum c_j integral_Zj eta^(n-1). Every degree is positive, hence all c_j vanish. Thus w-u and w-v are global pluriharmonic distributions and constants, so u-v is constant.

The required arXiv theorem query returned no direct textbook match, and the web fallback verified CADG Chapter III Corollaries 2.11 and 2.14 in Demailly's official 21 June 2012 PDF. Their normal-current, bidimension, order-zero, analytic-support, and lower-dimensional-remainder conditions exactly fit S. The argument adds no multiplier-ideal condition, divisor-class independence, bounded-mass or positive-lower-mass hypothesis, BMP, root-tail condition, nonlinear limiting argument, or claim about a singular maximizing current. The exploratory polytope draft was outside scope and was not used.
